Rashi on Megillah 16b:10:1.hebrew: עשרת בני המן ועשרת - הזכרת שמותן ותיבה הסמוכה אחריהן, כלומר: נשמתן נפלו כאחד:
Rashi on Megillah 16b:10:1.english: [The] ten sons of Haman and "ten" - [This refers to] the mentioning of their names and the word immediately following them; meaning, their souls departed as one:

Rashi on Megillah 16b:10:2.hebrew: זקיפא - פורק"א בלעז, בצד אחד זה למטה מזה:
Rashi on Megillah 16b:10:2.english: Zekifa [pole] - Forche [gallows] in Old French; [they were hanged] on one side [of it], one below the other:

Rashi on Megillah 16b:11:1.english: A half brick - This is the writing:

Rashi on Megillah 16b:11:2.hebrew: לבינה - הוא חלק שהוא כפליים מן הכתב, והאריח חצי לבינה:
Rashi on Megillah 16b:11:2.english: A whole brick - [It] is a blank [space] that is twice [the width of] the written [text], and the half brick is half [the size of] a whole brick:

Rashi on Megillah 16b:12:1.english: So that they should have no resurgence - That they should not have room to widen their steps beneath them:

Rashi on Megillah 16b:13:1.hebrew: מלמד שבא מלאך כו' - שהרי התחיל לדבר בלשון כעס, וסופו אמר "מה שאלתך":
Rashi on Megillah 16b:13:1.english: This teaches that an angel came, etc. - For he began to speak in an angry tone, and at the end [of his words] he said, "What is your petition":

Rashi on Megillah 16b:14:1.english: With the scroll - [meaning] that a scroll should be written before them at the time of reading:

Rashi on Megillah 16b:14:2.hebrew: הכי גרסינן אמר רב נחמן יאמר בפה מה שנכתב בספרים - ולא גרסינן "אמרה לו", והכי פירושה: סדר המקראות כך הוא — "וקיבל היהודים את אשר החלו לעשות", "כי המן בן המדתא האגגי וגו'", "ובבואה לפני המלך אמר עם הספר וגו'" — ומרדכי כתב אליהם שיעשו פורים כי המן ביקש לאבדם, ומה שבאת אסתר לפני המלך [להתחנן לו], כל זה יאמר שנה בשנה:
Rashi on Megillah 16b:14:2.english: This is how we read [the Gemara]: "Rav Nachman said: Let what is written in the letters be said by mouth" - And we do not read "she said to him." And this is its explanation: The order of the verses is as follows — "And the Jews undertook [to continue] what they had begun to do," "Because Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, etc.," "And when she came before the king, he said with the letter, etc." — [meaning that] Mordechai wrote to them that they should observe Purim because Haman sought to destroy them, and that Esther came before the king [to plead with him] — all of this shall be recited year after year:

Rashi on Megillah 16b:15:1.hebrew: כאמיתה של תורה - כספר תורה עצמו, שרטוט הלכה למשה מסיני:
Rashi on Megillah 16b:15:1.english: As the truth of the Torah - Like a Torah scroll itself; [the requirement of] scoring [the parchment] is a law [given] to Moses at Sinai:

Rashi on Megillah 16b:16:1.english: The matters of the fasts and their cry, and the decree of Esther - Thus are the verses juxtaposed:

Rashi on Megillah 16b:17:1.english: That they parted from him - because he neglected words of Torah and entered into [a position of] authority:

Rashi on Megillah 16b:18:1.hebrew: מעיקרא - בימי כורש, כשעלה (עם) זרובבל מן הגולה ומרדכי עמו, ונמנו בספר עזרא. כ"ד שנה היה בין מנין למנין, בימי כורש לדריוש האחרון. ולפי שנעשה מרדכי שר בינתים, ירד מחשיבותו אצל חכמים:
Rashi on Megillah 16b:18:1.english: Initially - [This was] in the days of Cyrus, when Zerubbabel went up from the exile, and Mordecai with him, and they were counted in the Book of Ezra. There were twenty-four years between [one] count and [the other], [from] the days of Cyrus to Darius the Last; and because Mordecai became a minister in the meantime, he declined in his stature among the Sages.

Rashi on Megillah 16b:19:1.hebrew: שכל זמן שברוך בן נריה קיים לא הניחו עזרא ועלה - שיש לך לתמוה למה לא עלה עזרא עם זרובבל בימי כורש עד השנה השביעית לדריוש האחרון לאחר שנבנה הבית, כמו שכתוב בעזרא: "ויבא ירושלם בחדש החמישי היא שנת השביעית למלך וגו'" (עזרא ז׳:ח׳); ובמדרש אמרו שהיה לומד תורה מפי ברוך בן נריה בבבל, וברוך לא עלה מבבל ומת שם בתוך השנים הללו; ודאמרן לעיל "ברוך נתנבא בשנת שתים לדריוש" — בבבל היה מתנבא ושולח ספרים לירושלים:
Rashi on Megillah 16b:19:1.english: For as long as Baruch ben Neriah was alive, Ezra did not leave him and go up - For you might wonder why Ezra did not go up with Zerubbabel in the days of Cyrus, [waiting] until the seventh year of the last Darius, after the Temple was built, as it is written in Ezra: "And he came to Jerusalem in the fifth month, which was in the seventh year of the king, etc." (Ezra 7:8); and in the Midrash [they said] that he was studying Torah from Baruch ben Neriah in Babylonia, and Baruch did not go up from Babylonia and died there during those years. And [as for] that which we said earlier, "Baruch prophesied in the second year of Darius" — he was prophesying in Babylonia and sending letters to Jerusalem.

Rashi on Megillah 16b:1:1.english: He should stumble in it - [This is the text] we read, and we do not read "his descendants":

Rashi on Megillah 16b:20:1.hebrew: יעקב למד תורה י"ד שנה בבית עבר - כשפירש מאביו ללכת לחרן, ולא נענש עליהן על כיבוד אביו; ובשאר כל השנים שנשתהה בבית לבן ובדרך נענש, כדמפרש ואזיל:
Rashi on Megillah 16b:20:1.english: Jacob studied Torah [for] fourteen years in the house of Eber - when he departed from his father to go to Haran, and he was not punished for them regarding honoring his father; whereas for all the other years that he lingered in the house of Laban and on the road, he was punished, as [the Gemara] goes on to explain:

Rashi on Megillah 16b:2:1.hebrew: כמה צוארין היו לו לבנימין - לא גרסינן, שכן דרך המקרא לכתוב "צוארי" לשון רבים, כגון "על חלקת צואריו" (בראשית כ״ז:ט״ז), וכן "בכה על צואריו":
Rashi on Megillah 16b:2:1.english: How many necks did Benjamin have - we do not read [this in the Gemara], for it is the way of Scripture to write tzavarei [necks] in the plural, [as in] "upon the smooth part of his neck [tzavarav]" (Genesis 27:16), [and] "wept on his neck [tzavarav]."

Rashi on Megillah 16b:4:1.hebrew: שיגר לו יין - לפי שדעת זקנים נוחה הימנו, זה הדבר הטוב לו מן הכל:
Rashi on Megillah 16b:4:1.english: He sent him wine - Because the elderly find it pleasing, this is the best thing of all for him:

Rashi on Megillah 16b:5:2.english: In its hour - if you see [that] its hour is successful:

Rashi on Megillah 16b:6:1.hebrew: תעלא - קרי' ליה יוסף לפני אחיו? מאי בצירותיה מאחווה:
Rashi on Megillah 16b:6:1.english: A fox - Are you calling Joseph [a fox] before his brothers? What is his inferiority to his brothers?

Rashi on Megillah 16b:8:1.english: "Light"; this is Torah - for Haman decreed against them that they should not engage in [the study of] Torah.

Rashi on Megillah 16b:8:2.english: This is a Festival - they took upon themselves [the observance of] the Festivals:

Rashi on Megillah 16b:8:3.english: This is circumcision - And [Haman] decreed against all of these:

Rashi on Megillah 16b:8:4.hebrew: אמרתך - זו מילה, שניתנה במאמר ולא בדיבור: "ויאמר ה' אל אברהם ואתה את בריתי תשמור" (בראשית י״ז:ט׳). ומצינו שדוד שמח עליה, שנאמר: "למנצח על השמינית" (תהלים ו); כשהיה בבית המרחץ וראה עצמו בלא תורה ובלא מצות, כיון (שנסתכל) במילה, שמח:
Rashi on Megillah 16b:8:4.english: Your word - This [refers to] circumcision, which was given through an utterance [ma'amar] and not through a formal commandment [dibbur]: "And God said [vayomer] to Abraham: As for you, you shall keep My covenant" (Genesis 17:9). And we find that David rejoiced over it, as it is stated: "For the conductor, upon the eighth [sheminit]" (Psalms 6:1); when he was in the bathhouse and saw himself without Torah and without mitzvot, once he looked at [his] circumcision, he rejoiced.

Tosafot on Megillah 16b:10:1.hebrew: צריך לאומרן בנשימה אחת - נראה דהיינו לכתחילה, אבל בדיעבד יצא:
Tosafot on Megillah 16b:10:1.english: One must say them in one breath - It appears that this is [only] from the outset, but after the fact one has fulfilled [his obligation]:

Tosafot on Megillah 16b:14:1.hebrew: אמרה מיבעי ליה - דמשמע דהכי קאמר: ובבואה לפני המלך, אמרה לו, מלבד הספר שעמו לעשות ולשלוח בכל המדינות, אמרה לו עוד: "ישוב מחשבתו הרעה"; דכיון דקאמר "בבואה אמר", משמע שיש לנו לומר מה שאמרה:
Tosafot on Megillah 16b:14:1.english: It should have said: “She said” - For it implies that this is what [the verse] is saying: And when she came before the king, she said to him — in addition to the letter that was with him to make and send to all the provinces — she also said to him, “Let his evil plot return [upon his own head]”; for since [the verse] says, “when she came... he said,” it implies that we should say what she said:

Tosafot on Megillah 16b:14:2.english: We will return to you, [chapter] Megillah Nikret:
